page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB per core, 50 GB of local SSD storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both ranking in the top tier. However, multi-core operations, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core tests, fall into the average range. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the weak category, though cached read-only memory bandwidth reaches 775.54 GB/sec. Large-block uncached read and write bandwidths are average at 44.55 GB/sec and 29.72 GB/sec respectively.

Due to its shared CPU allocation and starter classification, this instance offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, basic Redis deployments, and lightweight background tasks. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or heavy multi-threaded processing due to its shared resource model and lower memory performance tier.
